title: AlgoViz
text: Watch an algorithm think. Step through sorting, searching, graphs, and data structures at your own pace. Presentation: live. A collection of interactive algorithm and data-structure visualizations. A final sorted list hides the comparisons, swaps, and intermediate states that explain an algorithm. Vanilla JavaScript modules separate algorithm behavior from the interface. Playback turns intermediate states into something visitors can follow. A public visual playground spanning sorting, searching, graph algorithms, and data structures. Visual examples teach behavior; browser animation timings are not reliable algorithm benchmarks.

title: ASMBOOK
text: A notebook that lets you look inside the machine. Write 8086 assembly, inspect the CPU, and follow every instruction. Presentation: live. An interactive assembly notebook with lessons and an inspectable CPU. Assembly becomes easier to reason about when instructions, registers, and execution can be examined together. Preact and TypeScript organize the notebook interface. Browser emulation and execution views bring the low-level program into an accessible environment. A deployed browser notebook visitors can explore without installing a local assembly toolchain. An educational environment; emulator and lesson behavior should be evaluated for the particular instruction being studied.

title: Nano-Swarm
text: Guide a swarm through a simulated artery. Change the parameters and watch coordination emerge. Presentation: live. A browser-first educational simulation of coordinated microrobot-inspired agents interacting with a clot. Explain swarm coordination through a repeatable interactive model with visible controls and metrics. TypeScript separates deterministic simulation, rendering, guided playback, metrics, and exports. Three.js presents the pseudo-3D artery scene. The original application is built from a pinned source revision and hosted alongside this portfolio. Simplified educational visualization only: not a medical device, not patient-specific, and not predictive of treatment outcomes.
